text:
kevin: quick follow-up from the RFC review — thinking about a small refactor: introduce an authz 'scrubber' that runs before projection materialization, strips forbidden fields and rewrites predicates.
maya: scrubber how is different from the current prefilter?
sanjay: current prefilter lives in the query-gateway and gates queries; it rejects or accepts. scrubber would mutate requests to remove sensitive references so we can still serve more results instead of 403ing.
kevin: exactly. tradeoffs: + fewer blocked requests, + better cache hit reuse because responses are still usable; - increased CPU per request for rewriting, - complexity in correctness.
priya: main concern is auditability. If we rewrite queries we must keep original intent for logs + evals. otherwise compliance will scream.
kevin: agreed — plan: keep original query in an encrypted audit blob linked to request id (searchable via internal tooling), and emit a delta diff event for observability.
maya: perf wise: have we measured rewrite cost at p50/p99 for our typical dashboard queries? some panels run >100ms just for authorization checks today.
sanjay: did a quick local bench: rewriting predicate trees for a 200ms query adds ~8-12ms median, p95 ~35ms on c5.xlarge-like instances. biggest cost is predicate normalization and column remapping.
antoine: sounds plausible. caching nuance: if we mutate query we change cache keys. we could canonicalize mutated query to map to existing caches in many cases.
kevin: propose flow: 1) query arrives at gateway 2) authz scrubber runs (sync) 3) canonicalize for cache key 4) route to executor. fallback: if scrubber fails, gateway rejects — but we should canary a permissive mode where scrubber returns unmodified + flags a remediation event.
priya: canary + safety net: start with read-only dashboards only, and enable scrubber as pass-through with logging for 48h, then enable strict replacement behind a feature flag.
maya: ops ask: will this increase load enough to need autoscale policy changes for console fleet?
sanjay: likely small increase in CPU; we can offload heavy normalization to async prewarm for frequent queries (background canonicalizer). autoscale target change + CPU headroom for the first rollout.
ante: instrumentation: emit metrics: scrubber.latency, scrubber.mutations, scrubber.failures, cache.hit-after-scrub. also add a sampling of original vs mutated query for drift detection.
kevin: timeline idea: RFC follow-up PR with scrubber interface + shim in gateway (week 1), unit tests + benchmark harness (week 2), canary in staging with pass-through logging (week 3), enable strict mode on small tenant cohort (week 4-5).
maya: sounds good. assign owners? kevin -> design + PR, sanjay -> bench harness + perf tests, priya -> compliance + logging schema, antoine -> metrics + dashboards.
kevin: assign me too for rollout coordination. will open PR today with interface sketch and example rewrite cases. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: staging/console-gateway v2.14.0 -> 2026-04-02T03:00Z (canary).
priya: one last ask: please include end-to-end test that validates audit blob contains original query and obfuscated PII is stripped in mutation.
kevin: will do. thanks all.
